clue.text: Shocking news about a married American

indicators.note: about means going round, so the word for news is wrapped around the next pieces

parts.note: news is information, shortened to info
US is short for American, as in the US

explanation.surface: A scandalous report concerning an American who has recently wed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'news' looks like the subject of the sentence, but it supplies letters; the definition is the single word 'Shocking' at the start.
explanation.definitionFit: Something infamous is notorious for wickedness, so it is shocking.

clue.text: The brains of Archimedes are a help to a degree

indicators.note: the words 'brains of Archimedes' are said to help, by giving up the solution from inside their own letters

explanation.surface: Faint praise: the great Greek thinker's intellect is useful, but only up to a point.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer runs through 'braINS OF ARchimedes'. The indicator is loose: 'are a help' says those words assist the solver, and 'The brains' hints at something inside.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means to the extent that, limiting a statement to a certain measure.

clue.text: The most fancied competitor is in a pet

definitions.meaning: the runner the bookmakers expect to win, the one at the shortest odds
a person especially loved or indulged, like a teacher's darling

explanation.surface: The race's top tip turns out to be someone's darling.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both the runner backed to win and a person treated with special fondness.

clue.text: Game lost by the witless

definitions.meaning: a children's game played by rolling small glass balls
someone who has gone mad is said to have lost these, an idiom for sanity

explanation.surface: A game that only the foolish manage to lose.
explanation.definitionFit: Small glass balls form a children's game, and 'losing' them is an idiom for losing one's sanity.

clue.text: A shade of resentment

definitions.meaning: in an old sense the word means shadow or shade cast by trees
taking offence, as in the phrase 'take ...'

explanation.surface: Just a slight hint of a grudge.
explanation.definitionFit: From Latin umbra, shadow, the word once meant shade and now means offence taken.

clue.text: Fellow player's agent

parts.note: F is the abbreviation for Fellow, as in FRS
a player on stage is an actor

explanation.surface: Another performer's representative.
explanation.definitionFit: A factor is a commercial agent who buys and sells on behalf of another.

clue.text: Anatole catches fish, having no regular boss

indicators.note: catches means holds within, so the fish goes inside the surname

parts.note: Anatole France was a French novelist, so his surname is meant
an eel is a fish

explanation.surface: A man called Anatole lands a fish, being self-employed.
explanation.walkthrough: Anatole France (1844-1924) was a Nobel-winning French writer; his surname wraps round EEL.
explanation.definitionFit: A freelance works for many clients on contract rather than for one employer.

clue.text: Caught deserter with a butcher's knife

parts.note: C is the cricket abbreviation for caught
a deserter is one who leaves, a leaver

explanation.surface: A runaway soldier is captured carrying a meat chopper.
explanation.definitionFit: A cleaver is the heavy broad-bladed chopper a butcher uses.

clue.text: Muddle verbose witness

indicators.note: muddle means jumble, so the letters of the next word are mixed up

explanation.surface: Confuse a long-winded person giving evidence.
explanation.definitionFit: To witness something is to see or notice it.

clue.text: Up-river race between England and Wales

definitions.text: Up-river race between England and Wales

parts.words: Up-river race between England and Wales
parts.note: not a sporting contest but a rush of tidal water racing upstream along the river that forms the England-Wales border

explanation.surface: A cross-border boat race heading upstream.
explanation.walkthrough: 'race' suggests a contest, but here it is a fast surge of water; the river forms much of the border between England and Wales.
explanation.definitionFit: A tidal bore is a wave that rushes up an estuary, famously on this border river.

clue.text: Relax when going in the same direction

indicators.note: going in means entering, so the word for when goes between the two compass letters

parts.note: one compass point written twice, east and east, gives E and E
as can mean when, as in 'as I left'

explanation.surface: Unwind while travelling the same way as everyone else.
explanation.definitionFit: To ease is to loosen or let up, so to relax.

clue.text: Sign of luck for lover of careful disposition

indicators.note: disposition means arrangement, so the preceding letters are set out in a new order

explanation.surface: A lucky charm suits a lover who is cautious by temperament.
explanation.walkthrough: 'disposition' looks like temperament, but it signals rearranging all fourteen letters of 'lover of careful'.
explanation.definitionFit: Finding a rare clover with an extra leaf is a traditional omen of good fortune.

clue.text: Note to take legal action about one's second edition

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the note and the lawsuit word go round the next piece

parts.note: re is the second note of the sol-fa scale
to sue is to take someone to court
one is I, and 's adds S

explanation.surface: A memo threatening a lawsuit over somebody's second printing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Note' looks like a written memo, but it is the musical note of the sol-fa scale; 'second edition' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A book brought out again is a fresh printing, a second edition.

clue.text: The sort of joint everyone has

definitions.meaning: a coupling that lets a shaft turn at any angle, as in a car's drive shaft
something shared by all people, common to all

explanation.surface: Everybody owns a kind of joint.
explanation.definitionFit: A mechanical joint allowing movement in all directions bears this name, and the word also means common to all.

clue.text: Intensify a strain in race

parts.note: a breed is a race or stock of animals

explanation.surface: Strengthen a line of descent within a particular race.
explanation.definitionFit: To breed from closely related stock concentrates the traits of a strain.

clue.text: Meet opponents at the bar

parts.note: in bridge East and North sit on opposing sides, so E and N are opponents
a counter is the bar across which drinks are served

explanation.surface: Run into one's rivals over a drink in the pub.
explanation.walkthrough: In bridge, North-South play against East-West, so E and N are on opposite sides.
explanation.definitionFit: To encounter someone is to come across them, to meet them.

clue.text: Climbers are attached to this for training

definitions.text: Climbers are attached to this for training

parts.words: Climbers are attached to this for training
parts.note: the climbers are not mountaineers but plants, tied to a lattice frame that trains their growth

explanation.surface: Mountaineers rope themselves to something during practice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Climbers' suggests mountaineers; they are climbing plants, and 'training' is gardeners' word for guiding growth.
explanation.definitionFit: A lattice of light bars on a wall supports and guides growing plants.

clue.text: Sort of music the band played for Alexander

definitions.text: Sort of music the band played for Alexander

parts.words: Sort of music the band played for Alexander
parts.note: points to the 1911 Irving Berlin hit naming Alexander's band, which named the style of music it played

explanation.surface: A question about the music a band performed for someone called Alexander.
explanation.walkthrough: The song is Irving Berlin's 'Alexander's Ragtime Band' (1911).
explanation.definitionFit: The style is a syncopated American piano music of around 1900, the type named in the song title.

clue.text: Misinterpret one line of Pope

indicators.note: to misinterpret is to read wrongly, so the letters are read in a different order

explanation.surface: Misread a single line by the poet Alexander Pope.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pope' suggests the poet; here it is a pope named Leo, and the adjective means relating to him.
explanation.definitionFit: Leonine describes things belonging to a pope called Leo, such as the Leonine City in Rome.

clue.text: A short stalk in exercise to repel El Cid

parts.note: PE is physical education, exercise at school

indicators.note: to repel is to push back, so the name is written backwards

explanation.surface: A brief pursuit during a drill to fight off the Spanish hero El Cid.
explanation.walkthrough: El Cid is the medieval Spanish warrior hero; 'stalk' looks like a verb meaning to pursue, but it is a noun for a stem.
explanation.definitionFit: In botany and anatomy a pedicle is a small stem or stalk-like part.

clue.text: The usual fuss over a kiss — it sounds absurd, but it's true

definitions.text: it sounds absurd, but it's true

indicators.note: in a down clue over means placed above, so the earlier pieces sit on top of the kiss

parts.note: par is the normal or average level, as in 'on a par'
ado is fuss, as in 'much ado'
X is the cross written for a kiss

explanation.surface: Making the customary fuss about a kiss seems silly, yet is genuine.
explanation.definitionFit: A paradox is a statement that seems self-contradictory yet turns out to hold.

clue.text: Rashly deny one is the senior lady.

indicators.note: rashly means recklessly, so the letters are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: Recklessly refuse that someone is the eldest woman present.
explanation.definitionFit: A doyenne is the most senior or respected woman of a group.

clue.text: Move — hence an increase

indicators.note: move tells us to shift the letters of the next words around

explanation.surface: A change of position, and so a rise.
explanation.definitionFit: To enhance is to raise or heighten something, to increase it.

clue.text: Fruit tree under which seeds are found

definitions.text: Fruit tree under which seeds are found

parts.words: Fruit tree under which seeds are found
parts.note: the seeds are offspring: children were jokingly told babies were found under a certain fruit shrub

explanation.surface: A fruiting plant beneath which fallen seeds lie.
explanation.walkthrough: 'seeds' looks botanical, but means children: British parents once told children that babies were found under this shrub.
explanation.definitionFit: The shrub bears hairy green berries and is the traditional answer to where babies come from.

clue.text: Sewer where motorways merge.

parts.note: the M1 is Britain's main north-south motorway, written MI
a second M1, joining the first where the motorways merge

explanation.surface: A drain located at a motorway junction.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sewer' is one who sews: Mimi is the seamstress in Puccini's opera La Bohème. The M1 is a British motorway.
explanation.definitionFit: The heroine of La Bohème earns her living by embroidery, a seamstress.

clue.text: Small fish can be kept in this

definitions.text: Small fish can be kept in this

parts.words: Small fish can be kept in this
parts.note: 'can' looks like 'are able to', but also names the container itself, a can for little oily fish

explanation.surface: A place where little fish may be housed.
explanation.definitionFit: Small oily fish are packed tightly in a flat can of this kind.

clue.text: Chanced to behave ruthlessly

definitions.meaning: read as two words, to ..., fell being an old word for cruel or ruthless

explanation.surface: Took a risk in acting without mercy.
explanation.walkthrough: Split the answer as BE FELL: 'fell' is an old adjective for fierce or cruel, as in 'one fell swoop'.
explanation.definitionFit: An old verb meaning happened, and split in two it means to be cruel.

clue.text: 6 out of fifty gets the birch rod!

indicators.note: out of means outside, so the chopper goes round the letter for fifty

parts.note: the answer to 6 down is a chopper, here an axe
L is the Roman numeral for fifty
a birch is a tree

explanation.surface: Six out of fifty earn a caning.
explanation.walkthrough: '6' refers to 6 Down, a CLEAVER, taken as an AXE; 'out of' puts AXE round L, giving AXLE.
explanation.definitionFit: An axletree is the bar or rod on which a cart's wheels turn.
